text:
maria: Heads-up — started seeing multi-node TP jobs intermittently time out during steady-state inference after yesterday's kernel selector roll (fast_gemm_v2). First seen on prod-dedicated-3 cluster around 12:07UTC.
jon: seeing the same on a couple of 8-node runs, p99 token latency shoots up then one rank times out, job stalls.
pranay: logs show repeated NCCL timeout at the same epoch: "NCCL WARN NET/Connect: socket error" then ranks desync. Can paste stack.
ingrid: can you paste the exact kernel selector config? changed heuristics + batching right?
maria: yes, rollout changed kernel selector threshold for small sequences to prefer fast_gemm_v2 + enabled adaptive_batching_v2. config snippet:```
KERNEL_SELECTOR=fast_gemm_v2
ADAPTIVE_BATCHING=true
BATCH_WINDOW_MS=6
KV_CACHE_PREFETCH=on
```
jon: suspect interaction between smaller batch aggregation and the KV cache warmup pattern -> nodes try to allreduce uneven tensor sizes. profiling shows all-reduce latency spikes aligned with cache refill.
pranay: i captured perf traces from one run (attached below). key points: all-reduce RPCs within a step vary 2-10x, and CPU-side serialization waiting for KV lock observed. snippet:```
[perf] allreduce_duration_ms: [1.2, 9.8, 2.0, 7.6, 1.3]
[kv] kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.42
[kv] lock_wait_us: 1200
```
ingrid: wow 42% miss rate is high. which cache policy? LRU per-rank?
maria: LRU with per-rank warming and prefix caching, but adaptive batching reduced prefix amortization. earlier stable runs had miss_rate ~0.05.
sre-ops: deploy-bot indicates a canary-to-prod rollout at 11:45UTC (job: kernel-selector/fast_gemm_v2). culprit timeline matches.
deploy-bot: canary rollout: kernel-selector/fast_gemm_v2 -> 100% at 11:55UTC (triggered by ci/cd pipeline).
jon: repro locally by running the multi-node stress with small seqs (<32) and ADAPTIVE_BATCHING=true. repro script:```
./scripts/run_tp_stress.sh --nodes 8 --seq 16 --steps 500 --enable-adaptive-batching
```
pranay: quick triage idea: rollback kernel selector or force KV_CACHE_PREFETCH=off to see if miss_rate drops and stalls vanish.
ingrid: also try NCCL disable NCCL_NET=1->0 to force tcp path for debugging? set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and NCCL_SOCKET_NTHREADS=4.
maria: started a rollback to previous selector (stable_gemm) on staging; will run the same stress. posting logs in ~20m.
sre-ops: opened incident IR-2026-TP-01, assigning oncall.
pranay: i spun a repro with perf markers, attaching flame: most time spent waiting in allreduce_recv() on rank 3 when miss spikes occur. suspect imbalance in tensor sizes due to selective kernel padding.
jon: does our kernel selector sometimes alter pad behaviour? maybe fast_gemm_v2 introduced a different alignment that causes odd chunking across TP shards.
ingrid: yes it adds 128-byte packing for small dims which could change sharding boundaries. that explains uneven allreduce message sizes.
maria: confirm: when I force align=none, the problem rate plummets. test:```
KERNEL_ALIGN=none
```
pranay: ok that narrows it. plan: revert fast_gemm_v2 rollout, add a guard to avoid alignment changes for multi-node TP, and add a metric alert for kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.2.
jon: also add telemetry for per-allreduce message size variance and a rule to throttle adaptive batching when variance > threshold.
ingrid: created PR #4182 with the guard and metric. will run e2e.
maria: staging rollback shows stable 0.04 miss_rate and no timeouts in 2 runs. staging -> prod rollback pending approval from release lead.
sre-ops: approving rollback to 11:55 state, scheduling prod rollback in 10m.
pranay: follow-up actions: 1) add test to CI that runs TP stress for small seqs on 4-node, 2) add KV-prefetch opt-out in selector, 3) improve allreduce telemetry.
jon: i'll own the telemetry and throttle patch. ping me if you need a quick deploy.
ingrid: i'll lead the PR reviews for the guard.
maria: thanks. filing a short postmortem once prod rollback completes. for now, reverting rollout and monitoring. :thumbsup:
